source.title: Optimal Growth Schedules for Batch Size and Learning Rate in SGD that Reduce SFO Complexity

record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch-size and learning-rate schedules affect test accuracy, using a different empirical setup from the cited large-batch studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-accuracy curves for three schedule comparisons. It does not describe their test-accuracy outcomes in the text, so those results are recorded as figure-only. Gradient-norm and training-loss results concern optimization efficiency, not the held-out-performance measure named by V5.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out accuracy while varying batch-size and learning-rate schedules at a fixed 200-epoch budget. These comparisons bear on V5's recipe-adaptation component, although the supplied text does not preserve readable curve outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: appropriately coupled schedules improve convergence efficiency, and the authors claim they preserve generalization. The supplied text does not establish condition-specific test-accuracy differences supporting that latter claim.
record.recipe_differences: Studies schedule batch size and learning rate in mini-batch SGD, reporting convergence efficiency and test-accuracy curves; it does not reproduce the original large-batch comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size schedule and growth factor; learning-rate schedule and growth factor.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear batch growth with constant learning rate and suitably coupled exponential growth improve gradient-norm convergence and SFO efficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size and learning-rate growth schedules affect empirical-loss optimization efficiency; the critical batch size here minimizes computational cost, rather than identifying a held-out-performance threshold.

record.problems: Test-accuracy results are presented in figures without textual outcome descriptions or exact values; the reported range across three runs is not an error bar or confidence interval.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying test-accuracy rows were left out. Training gradient norms and training loss were excluded because they do not measure the held-out performance named by V5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of optimizer tuning.
Constant large versus constant small batches; workload-dependent penalty thresholds; longer-training remedies; warmup, normalization and regularization interventions; language-model settings.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. No directional verdict is justified from the supplied figure text: axis ticks and legends do not identify curve values or ordering, and the general concluding assertion does not resolve individual schedule comparisons. Missing numerical values are already represented by the cannot_determine rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare large and small batches under a fixed schedule and fixed epoch budget; tests ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 at 200 epochs under changing batch-size and learning-rate schedules.
